summary: Extend's C64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at Zoo 2015, a homage to the Aerial Core BBS of 1991–92. Code by Mankeli, music by Barracuda, graphics by Electric.
why: Sceners call it fresh and free of the usual mannerisms, embracing the machine with PETSCII and glitches rather than hiding it. Comments single out the transitions, the plasma and the final effect.

quote.text: A totally fresh approach and style, free from the usual mannerisms (sorry :-) Embracing the machine instead of trying to hide it, if you know what I mean.

summary: Illusion is a ZX Spectrum demo by X-Trade, with code by Dark and LD, graphics by Dark and Dangerous, and music by Deni. It won the ZX Spectrum demo compo at Enlight 1996.
why: It took first place in the Spectrum demo competition at Enlight 1996, so it's a good look at what a winning Spectrum demo from the mid-1990s offered.

summary: Hooy-Program's ZX Spectrum 16K demo with code, music and graphics by Gasman, which won the Oldskool Demo compo at Sunrise 2011. Effects play in a framed window beside the Justin Beeper logo while a scroller runs below.
why: A compo winner at Sunrise 2011 that fits in a 16K Spectrum and plays its soundtrack on the beeper, with one person, Gasman, behind all of it.

summary: A 16K Amstrad CPC intro by d0z with music by Mr. Lou, which won the Old School Executable Demo compo at Sundown 2012.
why: A compo winner at Sundown 2012, beating other old-school entries with a 16K CPC intro, and its source code has been released.

summary: An Atari 8-bit invitation intro for the Retrokomp / Load Error 2015 party, made by Wanted Team and Lamers with code by Szeryf, music by mCCnEx and graphics by At0m.
why: It won the Oldschool Intro compo at Riverwash 2015.

summary: Hooy-Program's ZX Spectrum 128K demo that won the ZX Spectrum 640k demo compo at Chaos Constructions 2013. Gasman handled code, graphics and music, with a font by Equinox.
why: It won its compo at Chaos Constructions 2013, and almost all of it is one person's work. It uses the Spectrum's multicolour mode to get far more colour on screen than the machine normally allows.

summary: A 256-byte ZX Spectrum intro by Skrju and Triebkraft, placed 4th in the 256b intro compo at Raww.orgy 2010.
why: Nominated for Most Original Concept at the Scene.org Awards 2010, a rare honour for something only 256 bytes long.

summary: Genesis Project's tiki-themed one-file C64 demo, winner of the Oldskool Demo compo at Edison 2013, with code and graphics by Mermaid, extra graphics by hedning and music by Stinsen. It plays as an endless loop.
why: Sceners single out Mermaid's hires graphics and animation, Stinsen's drum-heavy tune and how much is packed into a single file. Several also praise the final picture before the loop and the directory art.

quote.text: This is a perfect marriage of music, art and light-heartedness.

summary: Desire's Atari 8-bit demo, placed 5th in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2014. Code by Heaven, music by BeWu and Triace, and graphics from six artists including Alien, JAC! and Premium.
why: A full Atari 8-bit demo from a group better known on other machines, shown in a strong Revision oldskool compo and well received on Pouet.

summary: Censor Design's four-disk-side C64 demo, the fourteenth in their Wonderland series, placed 3rd in the demo compo at X 2023. It runs from a fractal intro through a KISS concert part to a sampled rap finale.
why: It won the 8-bit demo award at Siggraph Asia 2023 and was a Meteoriks nominee. Sceners praise the story tying the parts together, Talent's graphics, the smooth music design and above all the digitised rap end part.

quote.text: Pushing the edge with a rap part with so much visuals and the longest singing vocals I ever heard on the C64.

summary: Stardust's ZX Spectrum demo that won the ZX Spectrum demo compo at CAFe 2022, with code by Kowalski, psndcj and sq, graphics by Diver, 3D and animation by Rollerbob and music by Nik-O.
why: A first-place compo winner from a well-staffed Spectrum team, with dedicated credits for 3D and animation work alongside the pixel art and soundtrack.

summary: Eye-Q Team's ZX Spectrum demo, winner of the Retro Demo compo at Demosplash 2022, built around graphics by Grongy with music by Fatal Snipe and code by Z and Organism.
why: It took first place in the Retro Demo competition at Demosplash 2022, and its title puts graphician Grongy's artwork at the centre.

summary: Gemba Boys' underwater-themed ZX Spectrum 128K demo, which placed second in the Combined 8-Bit Demo compo at DiHalt 2014. Code by Busy, Noby, Mike and mborik, graphics by mborik and Ellvis, music by Aki.
why: A runner-up at DiHalt 2014 from a large Slovak crew, built around a single aquatic theme from start to finish.

summary: Performers' two-disk-side C64 demo, a tribute release that took 3rd in the C64 demo compo at X 2018, with code, graphics and music from a large cast including Bitbreaker, Mahoney, DeeKay, Jammer and LMan.
why: Sceners single out the music and its use of samples, and above all the greetings scroller part, which several call their favourite of the compo. Fast shaded vectors and a 50fps fullscreen cube also get praise.

quote.text: Right balance between fine design, hard effects and good flow. The final mod music screen is pretty awesome too.

summary: Crest's 1992 Commodore 64 demo, released at Christmas, with code by Crossbow and Vision and music from Deek, DRAX, JCH, MSK and Xayne. Expect border and sideborder scrollers, DYPP scrollers and a varying set of parts.
why: Sceners rate it for its VIC-II trickery and its soundtrack. They single out the multicolour brick wall in the borders with balls running through it, the DYPP part, and the way parts and the directory change between runs.

quote.text: I never saw a demo with more apparently impossible-to-do VIC-tricks.

summary: Skrju's ZX Spectrum demo, second in the ZX Spectrum 640K Demo compo at Chaos Constructions 2017. Flat-coloured shapes turn over a grey screen beneath bold, cheeky text captions.
why: A podium finish at Chaos Constructions, one of the main parties for Spectrum demos. It comes from Skrju, a well-known Spectrum group.

summary: Tristar and Red Sector Inc.'s VIC-20 demo for a machine with a 16K RAM expansion, placed 6th in the Console/Real Wild compo at Breakpoint 2010. Code and graphics by Streettuff, extra graphics by Veto, music by Linus.
why: A rare VIC-20 entry at Breakpoint from a long-running group, showing what the chunky low-resolution machine can do once it has extra memory.

summary: Vanity's Amstrad CPC intro from 2006, coded by Hicks with graphics by Beb and music by Tom&Jerry: a long snake of shaded balls weaves over a purple patterned backdrop while a scroller runs beneath.
why: Tagged as a sprites record, it pushes the number of moving balls the CPC can handle on screen. It's well liked on Pouët, with almost no dissent.

summary: Vanity's Amstrad CPC demo, the fourth in the Onescreen Colonies series, coded by Hicks with graphics by Beb and music by Zik, Tom et Jerry and e-dredon. It won the combined demo/intro compo at Benediction Coding Party #5 in 2025.
why: A compo winner that its own end screen bills as the close of the series, and it is on the Meteoriks 2026 watchlist.
highlights: credits from Hicks, Beb and three musicians

summary: Noice's first ZX Spectrum demo, a 48K production coded by Shadow with music by Yerzmyey, a logo by Piesiu and a font by Sy-Klone. It placed 3rd in the ZX Spectrum demo compo at Forever 2012.
why: A podium finish at Forever on the group's first outing on the Spectrum, with guest contributions from Piesiu of Agenda^Mystic Bytes and Yerzmyey of Hooy-Program.
highlights: character-block patterns in a framed window

summary: An Atari 2600 demo by Noice, coded by Shadow with music by Ilmarque, which placed second in the Atari 2600 demo compo at Silly Venture 2k11.
why: A second place in a dedicated VCS demo compo at Silly Venture, and a rare chance to see what a small team can draw out of the Atari 2600.

summary: Desire's Atari 800 XL/XE demo for 64K machines, fourth in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2016. Parts include voxel landscapes, a voxel sphere, a Wolfenstein-style part, a tilt/rotator and a Rescue on Fractalus-style mountain.
why: A packed showcase of 3D techniques on stock Atari 8-bit hardware, built by a large crew of coders and artists. An IRQ loader keeps music and effects running while the next part loads.

summary: Noice's demo for the Commodore 64 DTV, with code by Shadow, graphics by Rayden and music by 6R6. It won the Other Demo compo at Big Floppy People 2007.
why: An early multipart showcase for the DTV hardware. Sceners praised its filled vector in chunky mode, shadebobs and interference effects, and several said it felt like a mix of C64 and Amiga style.

quote.text: Feels like a mix between C64 and Amiga. Nice stuff. :-)

summary: A 256-byte intro for the Atari 8-bit by Ilmenit that won the Oldschool 256 Byte Intro compo at Lovebyte 2022: a monochrome forest of grey tree trunks shown in two side-by-side panels, with sound.
why: It won Lovebyte's oldschool 256-byte compo and then Best Oldschool Tiny Intro at The Nano Awards 2023, which puts it among the most recognised tiny intros on the Atari.

summary: A 32-byte Commodore 64 intro by Ate Bit, coded by 4mat: a glitch piece that churns colour blocks and character-set garbage across the screen while generating its own sound.
why: Sceners point out how much it gets from so little: by their count it fits into about 20 bytes, with what one calls "procedural" music and digi sound through $D418.

quote.text: impressive, 20 bytes with "procedural" music (so to say) :D

summary: Mahoney's C64 concept demo, placed 6th in the Demo compo at X 2014. Code and music by Mahoney, with graphics from Prowler, Redcrab and Mahoney, built around a sung song with a message.
why: Sceners single out the sampled vocals and the message, and note that the song is Mahoney's own rather than a cover. Several called it their favourite of the compo and a distinctly Mahoney style of demo.

quote.text: I hope Mahoney never stops, really original stuff, extra cool that it's not a cover either. And a message too ;)

summary: Oxyron's demo for the Commodore 64 DTV, winner of the Oldschool Demo compo at Nordlicht 2017. Code by Axis and Peiselulli, music by dEViLOCk and No-XS, graphics by Yazoo.
why: Sceners called it the best DTV demo so far. They single out the motion-blurred rotozoomer, the vector tunnel flights, the Gouraud-shaded vectors, the opening Oxyron logo and the music.

quote.text: The tunnels are exquisite and the first Oxyron logo (intro) is unbeatable! The music is also very nice!

summary: A 23-byte audio-visual intro for the Commodore 64 by 4mat of Ate Bit, released in a 32-byte intro category in 2011. It churns the screen into glitchy character garbage and colour blocks while playing a beat.
why: Sceners were struck that synced sound and visuals fit in 23 bytes, with praise for its clever use of kernal data in zero page and for how it improves the longer it runs. Its glitch aesthetic split opinion.

quote.text: Love it! It just gets better the longer you keep it running. Really clever stuff.

summary: Booze Design's Commodore 64 demo, released as a party version at Floppy 2005, where it took third place in the demo compo.
why: An unfinished party version of a Booze Design demo, as the "73%" in its title and the party-version tag suggest, placed third at Floppy 2005.

summary: A four-disk-side Christmas megademo for the C64, made jointly by Offence, Atlantis, Genesis Project, Lethargy and Bonzai under the name The Santas. It won the C64 demo compo at Forndata X-Mas 2020.
why: Sceners praise the festive mood, the graphics and above all the soundtrack of carefully made cover tunes. Commenters also note that dozens of contributors from several groups put it together in nine weeks.

quote.text: This certainly has a collection of beautiful graphics and solid effects, but for me the absolute highlight is the soundtrack. Each cover is extremely tasteful and lovingly crafted.

summary: Triad's C64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at Gubbdata 2018, coded by Houbba, Icon, Iopop and Powerslave with music by Dalezy and graphics by Twoflower.
why: Sceners praise how sleek and fluid it is, singling out the diagonal sideborder hires scroller, the transparency part and the hires starfield behind the final greetings. Several also call it a fine tribute.

quote.text:
totally did it for me again. really sleek and fluid!

and that starfield is about the greatest i know.

summary: HARD Software's Atari 8-bit demo, coded, drawn and scored by Téli Sándor alone, which won the Atari XL/XE demo compo at Silly Venture 2k17.
why: A one-man production that took first place in the Atari XL/XE demo competition at Silly Venture, the main Atari 8-bit party.

summary: An Amstrad CPC demo by Dirty Minds, coded by Optimus and Antitec with graphics by Optimus, Rex and Sice and music by Sice. It placed second in the Wild Demo competition at React 2003.
why: A second place in the React 2003 Wild Demo compo. This video shows the colour version, uploaded by the coder Optimus himself.

summary: Samar Productions' C64 demo, the finished 100% version of Dream Travel, marking 18 years of the group, with code by Hermit, doZe, Mr Wegi and Skull, graphics by Isildur and Skull, and music by Jammer and Randall.
why: Sceners saw it as a leap in design and coherence for Samar, praising its colourful, carefully animated parts, pixel-perfect graphics, smooth transitions and detail. Many single out the bitmaps and the isometric coffee mug.

quote.text: Everything on this demo looks awesome and is so well animated and pixel perfect. If only more demos were made with this kind of love and such attention to animation, transition and detail.

summary: Dentifrice's Atari 2600 demo, third in the Atari 2600 demo compo at Silly Venture 2k18, with code by Kezax, music by Glafouk and graphics from Exocet, Easy, Remdy and Logan Walters.
why: A podium finish in a dedicated VCS demo compo, and a sizeable graphics team for a machine this limited. It's tagged with a Space Invaders reference.

summary: Genesis Project's all-PETSCII C64 demo, with graphics and idea by Redcrab, music by Stinsen and code by Norrland. It won the C64 demo compo at Gubbdata 2016.
why: Sceners single out the detail Redcrab gets from the plain character set, the flow and storyline, Stinsen's soundtrack and the dancing alien. Several admit it changed their minds about PETSCII.

quote.text: These gfx have so much versatility and detail that I can't believe my eyes it's done with PETSCII!

summary: lft's solo C64 demo, with code, graphics and music all his own, which came second in the demo compo at Fjälldata 2025: a magician figure conjures nine coloured digit sprites that circle him and end up side by side, even in the upper border.
why: Nominated for Outstanding Technical Achievement at the Meteoriks. Sceners praise how it builds up the trick step by step, seemingly beating the eight-sprites-per-line limit, and admit they still can't work out how it's done.
highlights: digits moving into the upper border

quote.text: Great trick, that isn't immediately obvious, which is quite a feat on a platform where so many tricks have been done.

summary: Resource, Chorus and Singular's single-file C64 demo that won the demo compo at Árok 2012, with graffiti-style titles, a floor mapper and vector fonts. This is the 100% final version from November 2012.
why: Sceners single out how much it packs into one file, from the blocky sideborder plasma and wobbly kefrens to Soci's animated vector fonts.

quote.text: Great show for a one-filer. I especially liked the wobbly kefrens and the font.

summary: Gemba Boys' ZX Spectrum 128K demo that won the ZX Spectrum demo compo at Forever 2013, a group effort with code and graphics from a long list of contributors and music by Aki.
why: It took first place in the Spectrum demo competition at Forever 2013 and brings together a large Slovak and Czech crew, including Noby, mborik, z00m, Busy and UB880D, in one production.

summary: deMarche's ZX Spectrum demo that won the 8 Bit Demo compo at Multimatograf 2017, with code and graphics by TmK, extra graphics by KloyanA and music by Nik-O.
why: A compo winner at Multimatograf 2017 from deMarche. The video is the group's own no-flicker capture.
highlights: dithered portrait of a crowned face

summary: A ZX Spectrum demo by Cyberpunks Unity and Inward, coded by Elfh with music by Moran. It came third in the ZX Spectrum demo compo at Forever 2004.
why: A podium finish at Forever 2004, one of the main Spectrum parties of its day, from a collaboration between two groups. Elfh wrote both the code and the text.

summary: Darklite and Offence's 4K intro for the ZX Spectrum, with code by Neon, graphics by Pal and music by Response. It won the Oldskool 4K Intro compo at Revision 2026.
why: A first place at Revision in the Oldskool 4K Intro compo, beating the other size-limited entries across platforms.

summary: Micro is a ZX Spectrum 128K demo by Gemba Boys, coded by Noby, Busy, mborik and Mike with graphics by Ellvis and Aki and music by Aki. It came second in the ZX Spectrum Demo compo at Forever 2014.
why: A runner-up at Forever 2014 from a large Slovak crew pooling several coders. It's a solid example of the 128K Spectrum demo style of its time.

summary: Genesis Project's C64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at Flashback 2012: an animated pirate story with code, graphics and text by Mermaid and music by Mr. Death.
why: Sceners single out Mermaid's hand-drawn pixels and animation, the storytelling and the family-friendly charm, along with the cover of the pirate tune from Pippi in the South Seas.

quote.text: One can tell it's a labour of love. Instantly recognisable pixel goodness, and everything fits so well together. Makes it all look easy

summary: Fairlight's story-driven C64 demo, placed 4th in the demo compo at X 2006. Blocky robot characters act out a melancholic tale in stark black-and-white hires, set to Smalltown Boy's SID.
why: Sceners praise it as poetry rather than record-breaking: clean, artistic design, good flow and a melancholic story whose lyrics come from Dire Straits' Romeo and Juliet. Several felt it deserved better than 4th.

quote.text: Very artistic and clean. Good flow, accompanied by a great soundtrack. This proves that a demo is not all about breaking the most records.

summary: Ilmenit and Piesiu's 256-byte Atari 8-bit intro that won the Oldschool 256 Byte Intro compo at Lovebyte 2021: a little steam train crossing a desert under a streaked blue sky.
why: Won Best oldschool tiny intro at The Nano Awards 2022, and fits a whole scene plus sound into 256 bytes.

summary: Thesuper's ZX Spectrum demo that won the ZX Spectrum Demo compo at DiHalt 2011.
why: A compo winner at DiHalt 2011, and well received on Pouët.

summary: A 256-byte Atari 8-bit intro by JAC!, a silent wireframe cube turning over shifting background colours. It placed 6th in the Atari ST/800XL Demo/Bootsector compo at Outline 2011.
why: A tidy example of how much a 256-byte Atari intro can fit, and the source code is available for anyone curious about how it's done.

summary: Pers' Wastaiset Produktiot's VIC-20 demo, coded, drawn and scored by Viznut, which won the Oldskool Demo compo at Assembly 2002.
why: A compo winner at Assembly on one of the least-used 8-bit machines, made entirely by one person, Viznut, who handled code, graphics and music alike.

summary: Cluster's Atari VCS demo, released at Revision 2014, where it placed 4th in the Oldskool Demo compo. Code and design by Kylearan, music and player by KK, in a 32K cartridge.
why: A well-received Atari 2600 demo placing in Revision's oldskool compo, which shows how much a 2014 VCS production could still pull out of the console. Its stills show it doesn't take itself too seriously.
